correctness.rationale: Read the same 2026 primary Schubert surface paper at Sections 3.11, 4.3, 4.5-4.8 to verify the blow-up resolution, quotient singularities, exceptional curve contractions and total-transform intersection basis. For the iterated blow-up of P² at κ chain points on line at infinity, the classes satisfy B=H-ΣE, B²=1-κ, K_X=-3H+ΣE and -K_X=2H+B. Singular pencils contract only crepant -2 strings and have f^*(-K_Y)=2H+B, volume 9-κ, B-intersection 3-κ. For regular pencils κ>=2 the additional B contraction has discrepancy a=(3-κ)/(κ-1), yielding f^*(-K_Y)=2H+(2/(κ-1))B and volume 4κ/(κ-1). Nefness is checked on every irreducible curve: nonexceptional D distinct from B has H.D>=1 and B.D>=0; exceptional surviving terminal A has positive intersection; intermediate surviving A has zero; singular B has 3-κ. Klt quotient singularities and characteristic-zero basepoint-free theorem yield the weak-Fano/Fano and anticanonical contraction criteria. Independently checked exact rational intersection identities for all κ<=8 and selected size profiles; finite checks do not replace all-curves proof.

originality.rationale: Galgano–Gesmundo–Keneshlou (arxiv:2610.07164, posted October 5, 2026) completely establishes resolution, quotient types and intersection pairing. The new statement derives a sharp all-Kronecker-profile anticanonical nef/ample classification, volumes and contraction locus; no direct anticanonical classification appears in the inspected original sections. A nontrivial all-curves positivity argument is added, not merely renaming a published surface. However automatic use of source intersection data makes a possible unpublished corollary a residual risk.
residual_risks: An independent anticanonical corollary to the October 2026 surface paper could already appear in newer, unindexed geometric literature.
The explicit resolution and quotient singularity classification are credited to Galgano–Gesmundo–Keneshlou; their proof is used as a hypothesis and is not independently re-proved.
